blocks.text: 1.4 Approach and method
The study ran in four phases from November 2025, tested its hypothesis tree against the evidence of each workstream and took each figure from a ranked hierarchy of sources.
Four phases

The study ran in four phases: inception for one month, demand-side analysis for four and supply-side analysis for three (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p11). Enablement and final reporting ran for seven months, from May to the end of November 2026 (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p11, p12).

Each phase had a distinct job (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p11). Inception aligned expectations and ways of working and produced the Current State Diagnostic as a literature-based baseline (p14). The demand phase covered source markets, India and China route to market, benchmarks and trends; the supply phase covered spatial readiness and community inclusion, and the two overlapped from February to April (p12, p18, p19).

The final phase built the M&E framework, consolidated the strategy into this report and prepared the launch (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p22, p23). Three mechanisms governed the work: fortnightly working sessions with Wesgro, Steering Committee sessions at milestones and fortnightly written status updates (p27).
The hypothesis tree

The analytical core is a hypothesis tree, in which each entry names a lever on growth and is framed so the evidence could test it. Three pillars carry the tree: Reshape demand, Transform supply and Build enabling capability. Each pillar holds two themes, and the six themes hold twenty focus areas [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026, pp15 to 16: deck not in hand; page citation to confirm]. Nineteen of the twenty were tested against the evidence of a named workstream, and Appendix A1 traces each to the evidence behind it.

The tree disciplined the evidence. The stakeholder work coded each of its 223 insight statements to a pillar and a category of the tree before aggregating them (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5, p20 to p46). Because the study team did the coding, the counts show where views cluster; they do not on their own confirm a focus area.

The workstreams divide the tree between them. The demand and aviation work tested five of the six demand focus areas and the case for routes and seats. The infrastructure work tested cruise, mobility, product, visitor experience and capital. The inclusion work tested community inclusion and, with the stakeholder and infrastructure work, bookability. The stakeholder engagement supplied most of the evidence on climate risk, the flagship nature sites and the governance theme. The twentieth focus area, workforce and service skills, has no workstream yet. The 300,000-jobs ambition has no labour analysis behind it (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p4). Section 1.1 asks Wesgro and DEDAT to commission one in 2027.
Source hierarchy

Every figure in this report carries a source and page, and sources rank in five tiers. Where tiers disagree the higher tier wins; where two documents in one tier disagree, both values are recorded and the value used is stated with the reason. Nothing is reconciled by averaging.

Working analyses: the Market Assessment Report of May 2026 and the three Skift memos on digital and search insights (December 2025), segmentation (March 2026) and African markets (March 2026), cited by section.

Wesgro and government data cited through a deliverable (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p34): the Mero 2024 reports for all six districts, the Pero 2025 and the Growth for Jobs Strategy 2023. The same tier holds the Tourism Blueprint, Wesgro's five-year strategy and the StratEcon cruise liner economic contribution studies for 2023, 2024 and 2024/25.
Benchmark and reference reports, such as the UN Tourism barometer behind the global growth norm (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p7).
External public sources, used only where no higher tier carries the figure and labelled as such.

blocks.text: Two conventions follow. The MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment and the Skift memos are Word files without page numbers, so they are cited by section title. Summary material ranks below the deliverables: where the two differ, the deliverable's figure is used and the difference is logged.
Interim deliverables

Nine dated documents carry the evidence. Appendix A9 dates each by its cover and gives the version in hand and the SLA clauses it answers. Chapter 2 draws them together as one body of analysis in four parts: the global benchmarks and their lessons (2.1), demand (2.2), supply (2.3) and the enabling environment (2.4). The Inception Report frames 1.1 and 1.4, and the Current State Diagnostic frames 1.2. The Market Assessment Report of May 2026 is the working analysis behind the Demand-Side Analysis and alone prints the 2025 base the growth case uses (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p19).
Stakeholder engagement

Stakeholder engagement ran in four phases alongside the analysis (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p4, p17). Introduction and framing ran from January to March 2026, sense-making and validation in April and May, strategy socialisation in June and July and mobilisation from August into October. The Stakeholder Insights Report closed the first phase with insight tables for sixteen organisations, from Mossel Bay to the CTICC (p20 to p46). Sixteen is a count of those tables; the report prints no tally.

The method was strict about what an insight is. Sessions were run, insights extracted, each coded to a pillar and a category of the tree and then aggregated (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5). The 223 statements are the project team's paraphrases rated High, Medium or Low, not quotations, so this report attributes them to organisations and never to named individuals (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5, p20 to p46).

Two gaps in the record matter: phase 1 engaged no airline, online travel agent or tour operator, and the six demand-side engagements were proposed for phase 2 (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p16). [Open item: test the gateway and governance chapters with ACSA, the Cape Town Air Access airline partners, the City of Cape Town and Cape Town Tourism before Steerco.] The demand work drew instead on discussions with more than 20 stakeholders of its own (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p7). The outcomes of engagement phases 2 to 4 sit in no document in hand [Letsema to supply the phase 2 to 4 engagement record for Appendix A6].
Data limits

Five limits in the data shape how the findings read. The headline arrivals series counts international passenger arrivals at Cape Town International, not tourists, and Cape Town air arrivals stand proxy for the province in the market shares (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p25, p26, p29). No approved methodology exists for provincial tourism GDP and jobs, and no deliverable prints a Western Cape tourism employment baseline (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p37).

The supply dataset behind the Infrastructure Report (Supply_Infrastructure.xlsx) holds no geography below district, and its 17,195 records added after May 2026 are generated placeholders, as the study team found when it checked the file. [Open item: confirm whether the Infrastructure Report's count of 50,332 assets includes those records; if it does, restate Tables 1.2, 2.4 and A.18 and the district shares drawn from them.] The inclusion analysis runs on an OpenStreetMap asset layer, extracted on 16 September 2026, joined to Census 2011 sub-places, so its resident shares are fifteen years old (SME and Community Inclusion Plan, Sep 2026, p14 to p17, p22).

The growth model exists in two editions. The May Market Assessment runs from a 2025 base of 1,498,829 arrivals and the June Demand-Side Analysis from a 2024 base of 1,445,031 (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p19; Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p20). Both reach 2,175,778 in the base case and 2,516,282 in the accelerated case by 2035. The report runs the growth case from the 2025 base, keeps FY24/25's 1.44m as the recovery baseline and states which is which wherever both appear.
Completion plan

A six-week completion plan agreed on 12 October 2026 governs the last stage of the work. [Summary of Findings, 14 Oct 2026: six-week plan from 12 October, with weekly outputs and owners, to be inserted; deck not in hand.] The report goes to Steerco, Exco and the Board before the public launch in February 2027.
